newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $66.00-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $66.00-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Thursday were slow, with light sales reported at $66.00 per cwt, steady to down $1.00 from Tuesday's thin activity, USDA and feedlot sources said.

There were about 2,100 head of steers and heifers grading select and choice sold in Kansas, and about 200 heifers grading select and choice in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, USDA said.
Early outlooks for $67.00 cattle were diffused by weak beef prices at midday and talk that packers were using contract cattle for immediate cash needs, sources said.
Midday beef prices were quoted down $0.22 to $1.16 per cwt, with 163 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
Slipping beef prices were attributed to belief that most retailers were nearly done with booking orders for beef features over the next two weeks, they said.
Projections made before the New Year holiday on Wednesday for firm fed cattle prices faded as beef prices slipped, feedlot sources said.
Midday beef prices were quoted down $0.22 to $1.16 per cwt, with 163 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
Weakness in the beef market was attributed to ideas that retailers finished booking orders earlier this week for planned features into the middle of the month.
